code_actions.rationale: Claimed principal K85.90 (acute pancreatitis without necrosis) contradicts imaging and admitting assessment documenting 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and infected necrosis (H&P p.861; Discharge summary p.1085). Remove and replace with infected necrotizing pancreatitis code.

K85.11 denotes biliary acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis; the record documents infected pancreatic necrosis due to Klebsiella and procedures for infected necrosis (percutaneous drainage and VARD), so the uninfected-necrosis code is not supported.

Record documents infected/necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis (imaging and problem list) and a course of drainage and debridement; K85.82 (other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis) is the appropriate principal diagnosis and was present on admission per H&P and imaging.

No documentation of diverticulitis with perforation/abscess was found in the H&P, consults, or discharge summary; discharge problem list and hospital course document necrotizing pancreatitis and its complications instead (discharge summary p.1085).

The record identifies Klebsiella pneumoniae as the infecting organism. Policy maps Klebsiella pneumoniae to A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae); therefore recode A41.50 -> A41.53 and mark POA=Y (organism identified on admission/course).
Policy indicates that when an organism-specific sepsis code (A41.53) is assigned for Klebsiella pneumoniae, an additional B96.x organism code is not required; remove B96.1 as redundant.

0FBG3ZZ describes excision of pancreas via percutaneous approach; the operative note describes video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD), a debridement procedure, not a percutaneous pancreatic excision. The documentation does not support 0FBG3ZZ as billed.
CT documents cholelithiasis (multiple gallstones, CBD dilation). The billed K80.2 was flagged as heading-only ; recode to the appropriate FY2027 valid gallstone code (coder confirmation required).

system_note: What was billed: The claim lists K85.90 as the principal diagnosis with additional pancreatitis codes (K85.11, K85.82), sepsis codes (R65.21, A41.50, B96.1), respiratory failure/ARDS (J96.01, J80), AKI (N17.9), and multiple comorbidities; procedures include endotracheal intubation, prolonged ventilation, percutaneous drainage, VARD, feeding tube, PICC and lines (0BH17EZ, 0DH64UZ, 0FBG3ZZ, 0F9G30Z, 0W9G3ZZ, 02HV33Z, 03HY32Z, 5A1D90Z). What the record documents (key, auditable citations): - The admitting History & Physical documents imaging-confirmed necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology (History & Physical (Admitting), p.861). Evidence: Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n9, p.861] (ev1) - The same record lists infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae as an active problem and the discharge summary describes infected pancreatic necrosis treated with meropenem plus CT-guided percutaneous drainage (ICU day 13) and video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1085). Evidence: infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n1142, p.1085] (ev2); and Active Problem List entry 2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n9, p.861] (ev3) - The patient was vasopressor-dependent with elevated lactate on admission/early ICU care (supporting septic shock physiology): the Critical Care Progress Note documents vasopressor use and high lactate/P/F ratio (Critical Care Progress Note, p.946). Evidence: extremities cool; vasopressors on. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n11, p.946] (ev4); Lac: 5.0 | P/F 73. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n11, p.946] (ev13); H&P shows lactate 4.6 mmol/L on admission. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n9, p.861] (ev5) - The Pulmonology consult documents moderate-severe ARDS with pancreatitis as inciting event and the discharge note documents successful extubation on ICU day 18 (supporting ARDS and prolonged ventilation). Evidence: Moderate-severe ARDS with pancreatitis as inciting event. Responding to prone positioning. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n40, p.676] (ev14); Extubation was successful on ICU day 18 following resolution of ARDS. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n1142, p.1085] (ev15) - CT-guided percutaneous drainage and a retroperitoneal drain are explicitly described in the hospital course / discharge exam (supports percutaneous drainage codes and presence of a drain). Evidence: infected pancreatic necrosis ... CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 ... (same discharge summary). [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n1142, p.1085] (ev2); retroperitoneal drain in place with expected output. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n1142, p.1085] (ev7) - Endotracheal intubation is documented with RSI and radiographic confirmation (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p.44) and the chest x-ray documents ETT position. Evidence: RSI with etomidate and rocuronium. Placement confirmed clinically and radiographically. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n16, p.44] (ev8); Endotracheal tube tip 4 cm above the carina. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n14, p.56] (ev12) - Enteral nutrition and a PEG/jejunal feeding route are shown in the chart (enteral feeding maintained via nasojejunal tube; PEG site noted at discharge) (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1085). Evidence: Enteral nutrition was maintained via nasojejunal tube throughout the critical phase. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n1142, p.1085] (ev6) Policy requirements and how the record compares: - Principal diagnosis sequencing: The admission H&P, ED note and consults identify the reason for admission as severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis (not simple acute pancreatitis without necrosis). The billed principal K85.90 (acute pancreatitis without necrosis) contradicts the record's imaging and admitting assessment; the principal should reflect the necrotizing/infected pancreatitis that occasioned the ICU admission (History & Physical (Admitting), p.861; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1085). [ev1, ev2] - Infected necrosis vs. uninfected necrosis: The record documents infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and percutaneous drainage + VARD; this supports coding for infected necrosis (K85.82) and organism-specific sepsis coding (A41.53) rather than K85.11 (biliary with uninfected necrosis) or K85.90 (no necrosis). [ev2, ev3, ev9] - Sepsis/septic shock validation (R65.21): the governing policy requires provider documentation of sepsis/septic shock OR objective criteria (vasopressor use + lactate >2 after resuscitation) and organism identification where applicable. The chart documents vasopressor therapy, lactate >2 (4.6-5.0 mmol/L), markedly elevated procalcitonin and organ dysfunction (respiratory failure, AKI) consistent with severe sepsis/septic shock and documents Klebsiella as the infecting organism. These meet the policy's validation criteria for R65.21 and organism-specific A41.5x coding (Policy: vasopressor requirement and lactate >2 criterion; Policy: Klebsiella -> A41.53). [ev4, ev5, ev13, ev2, RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b101 (Criterion 2), RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b93 (lactate), RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b81-r9 (A41.53 mapping)] - Organism-specific sepsis coding: Policy table maps Klebsiella pneumoniae to A41.53 and indicates that an additional B96.x organism code is not needed when the A41.53 is used (Policy). The claim's use of A41.50 (Gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) + B96.1 (Klebsiella) is inconsistent with the policy guidance and culture/clinical documentation that identifies Klebsiella. [RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b81-r9] (ev9) - Procedure-technique mismatch: The discharge summary documents video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) (a surgical debridement), whereas the billed 0FBG3ZZ is Excision of pancreas, percutaneous approach. The documentation supports percutaneous drainage (CT-guided) and VARD (surgical debridement), not a percutaneous excision of the pancreatic parenchyma. Therefore 0FBG3ZZ is not supported as billed; the percutaneous drainage code (0F9G30Z) and other vascular/line/ventilation codes are supported. [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_14.pdf-n1142, p.1085] (ev2) Determination and corrective action summary (claim-level): - Finding: The principal diagnosis K85.90 (acute pancreatitis without necrosis) is not supported and must be removed; the record documents necrotizing, infected, gallstone pancreatitis and infected pancreatic necrosis (supporting K85.82) and this should be the principal diagnosis. [ev1, ev2] - Finding: Sepsis coding should be revised to organism-specific sepsis A41.53 (Klebsiella pneumoniae) rather than A41.50, and the B96.1 organism-only code should be removed because the organism is embedded in A41.53 per the policy mapping. R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) is supported and appropriately carries MCC severity given the documented vasopressor requirement and lactate >2. [ev2, ev4, ev5, ev9, RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b93, RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b101] (ev9, ev11, ev10) - Finding: The billed pancreatic procedure 0FBG3ZZ (Excision of pancreas, percutaneous approach) is not supported by the operative descriptions (VARD = debridement) and should be removed (no direct substitute code present in retrieved data). CT-guided percutaneous drainage (0F9G30Z), and other billed line items (ETT insertion, prolonged mechanical ventilation, PICC, arterial line, drainage of peritoneal/retroperitoneal cavity) are supported by the record and will be retained. [ev2, ev8, ev12, ev6, ev7, ev15] Caveats: All changes above are based solely on the retrieved chart notes and the retrieved sepsis and respiratory-failure policy documents. Discharge disposition note lookup returned no structured UB-04 discharge code to report; transfer to LTAC is documented in the discharge/transfer summary but get_discharge_disposition_note returned no rows so no UB-04 code is recorded in this audit package. rationale_letter: To: Medical Records / Coding Department Re: Audit determination for inpatient claim MR_14 (Admission 05/29/2026-10/10/2026) We completed a DRG audit of claim MR_14. After review of the medical record and applicable coding policy, we find the claim requires correction (Finding). Basis for finding: 1) Principal diagnosis sequencing: The admitting History & Physical and imaging document severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis (History & Physical, p.861). The discharge summary and problem list document infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1085). The billed principal code K85.90 (acute pancreatitis without necrosis) is not supported by this documentation. The correct principal diagnosis is the infected necrotizing pancreatitis documented in the chart. 2) Sepsis coding and organism specificity: The chart documents vasopressor-dependent shock with lactate >2 mmol/L (Critical Care Progress Note, p.946; History & Physical, p.861) and identifies Klebsiella pneumoniae as the causative organism (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1085). Policy requires organism-specific sepsis coding when the organism is identified; the mapping within the policy indicates Klebsiella pneumoniae -> A41.53 and that a separate B96.x organism-only code is not required when A41.53 is used. Therefore A41.50 and B96.1 as billed are incorrect - the sepsis code should be A41.53 and B96.1 removed. R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) is supported by documented vasopressor use and elevated lactate and remains an MCC where present. 3) Procedure/technique mismatch: The chart documents CT-guided percutaneous drainage and video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1085). The billed ICD-10-PCS 0FBG3ZZ (Excision of pancreas, percutaneous approach) denotes excision of pancreatic tissue via a percutaneous approach and is not supported by the operative description of VARD (debridement). Therefore 0FBG3ZZ should be removed; percutaneous drainage (0F9G30Z) and other line/ventilation codes remain supported. Corrections being made: - Principal diagnosis changed from K85.90 to K85.82 (other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis) as principal. - Replace A41.50 with A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae); remove B96.1 as redundant per policy guidance. - Retain R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) given documented vasopressor requirement and lactate elevation. - Remove K85.11 and K85.90 (codes indicating uninfected or no necrosis) as not supported by imaging and operative course. - Remove procedure 0FBG3ZZ (Excision of pancreas, percutaneous approach) as unsupported by the operative documentation (VARD described). Keep procedures supported by notes (endotracheal intubation and ventilation, percutaneous drainage, PICC/lines, prolonged ventilation). Key evidence cited (examples): - History & Physical (Admitting), p.861: Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology. - Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1085: infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16; extubation ICU day 18. - Critical Care Progress Note, p.946: vasopressors on; Lac: 5.0; P/F 73. - Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p.44: RSI with etomidate and rocuronium. Placement confirmed clinically and radiographically. - Sepsis policy (Validation Criteria): vasopressor requirement + lactate >2 and organism-specific coding rules (Klebsiella -> A41.53). If you disagree with these changes, please provide the specific clinical documentation (dated and signed provider note or lab/culture result with provider attribution) showing either (a) an explicit, dated provider statement that the principal reason for admission was sepsis (which would alter principal sequencing) or (b) documentation that the pancreatic necrosis was definitively uninfected and no organism-specific sepsis diagnosis applies. Absent that documentation, the corrections listed above will stand. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor
